# The Long Silence of Light

## Scripture

**"But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession, that you may declare the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light." — 1 Peter 2:9**

## Reflection

On a clear November night, look up and you'll notice something humbling: most of the stars you see may no longer exist. Their light has traveled for hundreds or thousands of years, arriving only now—long after the fire that made it has gone out. We call it "light lag," and it means the night sky is a kind of archive, a record of faithfulness we're still receiving.

Peter writes that we've been called *out of darkness into wonderful light*. But notice what he says next: we are called to *declare* that light—to become, ourselves, a kind of light-lag, a witness that arrives after God's initial work and keeps arriving for generations to come.

For much of history, the light of the gospel has reached people through the faithfulness of those who came before—parents, saints, strangers whose names we'll never know. The same is true of us. The small kindness you offer, the quiet integrity you keep, the hope you hold onto in a hard season—these travel further than you can see. You may never witness their arrival. But light doesn't need an audience to keep traveling.

This fall, as the skies darken early, remember: you are not the source of the light. But you are its messenger—and the message is still on its way.

## Prayer

Lord, thank You for calling us out of darkness into Your wonderful light. Make us faithful messengers of that light, even when we cannot see where it lands. May what we reflect of You keep traveling long after our moment has passed. Amen.
